short: Sixty-three years in which Britain industrialised and the monarchy went ceremonial.
full:
Victoria became queen at eighteen in June 1837 and married her cousin Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha in 1840. Albert shaped both the court and the crown's public role, promoting the Great Exhibition of 1851 and pushing the monarchy towards political neutrality. His death from typhoid in 1861 sent her into a seclusion so prolonged that it revived republican criticism.

Her reign covered the railway boom, the Reform Acts of 1867 and 1884, the Irish Home Rule crises, the transfer of Indian government to the crown after the rebellion of 1857, and the scramble for Africa. She was proclaimed Empress of India in 1877 and returned to public life through the jubilees of 1887 and 1897. By her death at Osborne House in January 1901 the sovereign's power had narrowed to Bagehot's rights to be consulted, to encourage and to warn, and her children and grandchildren sat on or beside half the thrones of Europe.
